title: CrossRAT_Investigation_428
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential CrossRAT infection on a target system. CrossRAT is a backdoor malware capable of remote access and control, data exfiltration, and maintaining persistence on infected systems. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the threat.
outcomes: Analyze network communication for command-and-control (C2) activity.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential CrossRAT infection on a target system. CrossRAT is a backdoor malware capable of remote access and control, data exfiltration, and maintaining persistence on infected systems. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target system via SSH using the provided credentials.
levels.local_content: Access the target system via SSH using the provided credentials.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the target system, you notice unusual network activity. Investigate the running services on the target system to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services. The flag type is a service name.
levels.solution: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services. The flag is the name of the suspicious service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the list of running services and look for any that seem out of place or unfamiliar.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service name is a systemd service file. Look for files ending in .service in the /etc/systemd/system directory.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Now that you have identified a suspicious service, determine how it is automatically started after a system reboot. This will help you understand the persistence mechanism used by the malware. The flag type is a timer name.
levels.solution: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all systemd timers. The flag is the name of the timer associated with the suspicious service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate systemd services and timers to find any related to the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all systemd timers.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The persistence mechanism is a systemd timer file. Look for files ending in .timer in the /etc/systemd/system directory.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: Analyze the network traffic associated with the suspicious service to determine which port is used for command-and-control (C2) communication. This information is crucial for containing the threat. The flag type is a port number.
levels.solution: Use the command `ss -tulnp` to list all listening ports. The flag is the port number used for C2 communication.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use network monitoring tools to inspect the traffic and identify the suspicious port.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ss -tulnp` to list all listening ports.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for a port that is not commonly used by standard services. The suspicious port is likely to be a high-numbered port.
